im-c55-01.h: -던 (Past Repeated Habit / Interrupted State) vs -(으)ㄴ (Past Completed Action)

a.d: Modifies a noun to describe an action repeatedly done in the past, or started but left unfinished.
ex: 어릴 때 친구들과 자주 **놀던** 골목길이에요. — This is the alley where I used to play often with friends when I was young.

b.d: Modifies a noun to describe a one-time event that took place and finished completely in the past.
ex: 어제 도서관에서 **빌린** 책을 다 읽었어요. — I finished reading the book that I borrowed from the library yesterday.

im-c55-01.tip: Use -던 for recurrent memories, habits, and unfinished tasks; use -(으)ㄴ for completed past actions.

im-c55-01.q: Fix the unnatural sentence that incorrectly uses completed past -(으)ㄴ when recalling a restaurant frequently visited during university.
im-c55-01.wrong: 여기가 대학교 때 매일 밥을 먹은 단골 식당이에요.
answers: 여기가 대학교 때 매일 밥을 먹던 단골 식당이에요.
여기가 대학교 때 매일 밥을 먹던 단골 식당이에요
여기가 대학교 때 자주 가던 단골 식당이에요.
여기가 대학교 때 자주 가던 단골 식당이에요
im-c55-01.hint: When modifying a regular hangout or habitual past action, use the recollection modifier -먹던 or -가던.
im-c55-01.why: Habitual past routines and familiar places require the recollection form -던 rather than simple completed past -(으)ㄴ.

im-c55-02.h: -더라고요 (Vivid Firsthand Experience) vs -대요 / -다고 해요 (Hearsay / Indirect Report)

a.d: Used when the speaker directly experienced, saw, or tasted something and conveys that discovery vividly.
ex: 어제 그 식당에 가 봤는데 밑반찬이 정갈하고 아주 **맛있더라고요**. — I went to that restaurant yesterday and the side dishes were neat and really delicious.

b.d: Used when conveying information heard indirectly from others without personal experience.
ex: 그 식당은 밑반찬이 정갈하고 아주 **맛있대요**. — I hear that restaurant has neat side dishes and is very delicious.

im-c55-02.tip: Use -더라고요 only for your own firsthand experiences; use -대요 for what others told you.

im-c55-02.q: Fix the error where -더라고요 is unnaturally applied to describe the speaker's own internal emotional feeling.

answers: 어제 영화의 슬픈 장면을 보고 제가 너무 슬펐어요.

어제 영화의 슬픈 장면을 보고 눈물이 나더라고요.
어제 영화의 슬픈 장면을 보고 눈물이 나더라고요
im-c55-02.hint: Internal feelings of the speaker take standard past tense -슬펐어요, or observable reactions take -눈물이 나더라고요.
im-c55-02.why: -더라고요 cannot be used to observe one's own internal emotional states as if watching from the outside.

im-c55-03.h: -던데요 (Trailing Off to Prompt Reaction) vs -더라고요 (Clear Declarative Recollection)

a.d: Delivers an observed fact while leaving the end of the sentence open to invite the listener's response or confirmation.
ex: 아까 보니까 사무실에 불이 켜져 있**던데요**? — Seeing earlier, the office light was turned on?

b.d: Delivers a personal experience clearly with strong finality without expecting an immediate conversational turn.
ex: 사무실에 가 보니까 불이 켜져 **있더라고요**. — When I went to the office, the lights were on.

im-c55-03.tip: Use -던데요 to prompt the listener to join the conversation; use -더라고요 to report your own findings decisively.

im-c55-03.q: Fix the sentence that unnaturally tags a blunt directive onto the gentle observational ending -던데요.
im-c55-03.wrong: 아까 그 서류 복사기 옆에 놓여 있던데요, 지금 찾도록 하세요.
answers: 그 서류 아까 복사기 옆에 놓여 있던데요.
그 서류 아까 복사기 옆에 놓여 있던데요
그 서류 아까 복사기 옆에 놓여 있던데요?

im-c55-03.hint: End gently with -던데요 to let your colleague naturally react without being commanded.
im-c55-03.why: -던데요 is a gentle communicative ending that leaves room for the interlocutor to respond naturally.

im-c55-04.h: -더라고요 (Vivid Review / Definite Discovery) vs -던데요 (Gentle Observation Inviting Reaction)

a.d: Used to share a clear personal review or finding with firm confidence.
ex: 어제 본 영화는 배우들 연기가 정말 **감동적이더라고요**. — In the movie I watched yesterday, the actors' performances were truly touching.

b.d: Used to convey an observation gently, allowing room for the listener to chime in or react.
ex: 어제 그 영화 보니까 상영관에 관객이 꽉 차 **있던데요**? — When I watched that movie yesterday, the theater was packed with audiences?

im-c55-04.tip: Use -더라고요 to state reviews; use -던데요 to invite interactive dialogue.

im-c55-04.q: Fix the unnatural sentence that incorrectly uses completed past -(으)ㄴ to modify a winter coat worn repeatedly last season.

im-c55-04.hint: For habitual clothing worn repeatedly throughout a past period, use the recollection form -입던.
im-c55-04.why: Actions that were repeatedly done across a past duration require the recollection modifier -던.
